data.hypothesis: An 8x16 register-tiled AVX-512 FMA kernel should accelerate the large GEMM relative to the measured serial baseline. B-only 128x128 panels may improve reuse for larger matrices, but their per-call allocation and packing cost could offset that benefit; the same tile kernel uses direct B access below a generic two-panel threshold. A later matched-size direct-versus-packed run is needed to isolate the packing effect.
data.notes: No failed candidate attempts or candidate measurements are present in the supplied history. The baseline is correct and its n=1024 native timings were 5.828249351, 5.612412845, and 5.692197808 seconds (mean 5.710953335 seconds). This candidate's correctness and repeated timings remain for controller evaluation; no speedup is claimed. Packing is B-only to isolate that choice, and the allocation/copies occur inside run.
transformations: Replace fixed-size scalar GEMM with generic 8-row by 16-column output tiles and explicit AVX-512 FMA microkernel, guarded by runtime AVX-512F/FMA detection; use a scalar fallback for unsupported targets and row tails.
Assign disjoint output row/column tiles to an OpenMP team clamped to at most eight threads.

Use direct B access for dimensions below two 128-column panels; for larger dimensions, allocate a per-call 128x128 B-panel buffer, pack each K/column panel, and reuse the same microkernel across row tiles.

Initialize each output tile from zero on the first K panel and accumulate later panels, ensuring all output elements are overwritten on every invocation and handling K, row, and column tails generically.
